topics.headline: California's Title III EL RFA is live — the money is on the table, and most of our partners aren't reaching for it
topics.why_matters: Five active partners (Ocean Grove, South Sutter, Visions, Heartland, Pacific Coast Academy) have confirmed Title III Immigrant receipt; 18 partners have never applied; two schools on the pipeline (Community Collaborative Charter, Cabrillo Point) have unspent Title III Immigrant funds sitting there. An RFA release with an application window is the single most actionable Category A signal of the past two weeks, and it lands during a federal moment where "the proposed 2025–2026 federal budget would eliminate Title III entirely, cutting almost $890 million in supports for MLs" — meaning California's state-administered Title III window may be the last clean draw before federal contraction.
topics.angle: "The Title III RFA is live. Here's the 3-question checklist every EL coordinator should run this week." Anchor to A+'s LTEL reclassification case data.
topics.roman_take: The compliance angle is a distraction — the real question is whether your intervention plan can *spend the money on something that reclassifies kids*, because Title III's political runway is shrinking and unspent dollars are the fastest way to lose future access.
topics.danielle_take: Walk through the practical Title III workflow — application timing, allowable use categories, and how to structure a small-group EL intervention scope that survives a CARS audit.

topics.headline: iLEAD Flex opens as the 7th school in the iLEAD network — NCB moratorium lift is now producing real charter expansion
topics.category: C (Tier A partner expansion — iLEAD network) + A (state charter policy)
topics.why_matters: iLEAD is a Tier A partner (iLEAD Hybrid, Online, Exploration, Lancaster, Antelope Valley — plus APLUS+ member). The Antelope Valley Union High School District board unanimously approved the charter petition for iLEAD Flex, the seventh school in the iLEAD network, integrating project-based curriculum with social-emotional learning across a tuition-free TK-12 model. The California moratorium on new non-classroom-based (NCB) charter schools was lifted this year, and iLEAD is now expanding into new communities under its tuition-free TK-12 model spanning classroom-based, hybrid, online, and independent home study. This is a direct partner-expansion signal in a cluster A+ already serves, and it opens a warm door on intervention services for the new site.
topics.angle: Celebrate iLEAD's expansion as evidence that flex-based, learner-centered charter models are meeting real demand in Lancaster — and remind the market what strong intervention plumbing has to be in place from day one at a new NCB site.
topics.roman_take: The NCB moratorium lift is a stress test — networks that scale without ESSA-aligned Tier 2/3 intervention baked into the launch will hit an accountability wall by year two.
topics.danielle_take: When a new NCB campus opens in August, the operational question isn't "do we have tutoring vendors?" — it's "is our intervention delivery documented to the standard CARS will ask for next spring?" — and here's how iEM partners already have that answer.

topics.headline: Varsity Tutors just walked away from the K-12 schools market. What that tells charter directors about the "platform tutoring" bet.
topics.why_matters: At the end of July, Varsity Tutors — one of the nation's largest virtual tutoring providers — told its school customers it would discontinue Varsity for Schools effective immediately, and in a shareholder letter said the decision would let it shift focus back to its original consumer model selling directly to parents and college students. Matthew Kraft, a Brown University education and economics professor who has studied and evaluated tutoring programs serving public school districts, said the move signals a shift in the tutoring market that K-12 will continue to see unfold. This is the single highest-differentiation moment A+ will get all quarter: a top-of-market competitor is publicly admitting the mass-virtual, platform-tutoring model doesn't work well enough in schools to keep running. A+ has spent years building the opposite model — embedded, human, relationship-based, tied to Title III and MTSS. Charter directors reading this news are asking themselves right now: "What does our tutoring vendor's business model actually incentivize them to do next year?" A+ has an answer only A+ can credibly give.
topics.angle: "The country's biggest virtual tutoring platform just told districts it's done. Here's what we think that means for charter schools that are still building their intervention model for 25-26." Then a short list of what to look for in a partner that isn't structured around the same exit incentives.
topics.roman_take: Conviction cut — "This is what happens when the growth story matters more than the student. Charter schools were the harder customer, so they got dropped. We built A+ the opposite way." Direct, no hedging.
topics.danielle_take: Implementation cut — What she's already telling her partner schools (Ocean Grove, South Sutter, Visions, Heartland, Pacific Coast Academy) about vendor risk when Title III and Title I dollars are on the line, and the operational questions a Special Programs Coordinator should be asking their current tutoring provider this month. ---
